title: The Community
description: Ten short stories about life in small American towns: a town meeting, a local news website, a food bank, the high school football team, a new fish restaurant, music in the park, helping a neighbor, planting trees, a new family's first job and a block party.

lessons.title: The Town Meeting
lessons.summary: The people of Millbrook meet and choose between a new park and a new parking lot.
lessons.text:
Lena lives in Millbrook, a small town in Ohio. The population of Millbrook is about 4,000 people. The population is small, but the people really care about their town.

This year, the town has some money for a new project. There are 2 options. The first option is a new park. The second option is a new parking lot near the shops on Main Street.

A committee of 5 people has to choose one option. But first, the committee wants to hear the opinion of the people. So the committee plans a town meeting.

Lena goes to the meeting with her friend Sam. The room is full. Everyone wants to give an opinion.

Ruth, the head of the committee, speaks first. "The purpose of this meeting is simple," she says. "We want to hear your opinion. We aren't here to choose today. We are here to listen."

A man asks a specific question. "How much money does each option require?" Ruth gives specific numbers. "The park requires $200,000. The parking lot requires $150,000."

Some people like the park. "Our children need a place to play," a woman says. Other people like the parking lot. "There aren't enough places for cars on Main Street," a man says.

Then Lena gives her opinion. "I considered both options," she says. "A parking lot can help the shops. But a park is good for everyone: children, parents and old people." Many people agree with her.

At the end, the committee asks everyone to vote. 70 percent of the people vote for the park. 30 percent vote for the parking lot.

Ruth is happy. "The committee considered every opinion," she says. "70 percent is a clear answer. Millbrook is going to have a new park." Lena and Sam walk home happy.

Questions:
What is the population of Millbrook?
The population of Millbrook is about 4,000 people.
What are the 2 options?
The first option is a new park, and the second option is a new parking lot.
What is the purpose of the meeting?
The purpose of the meeting is to hear the opinion of the people.
How much money does the park require?
The park requires $200,000.
What percent of the people vote for the park?
70 percent of the people vote for the park.

lessons.title: News for Pine Hill
lessons.summary: Linda starts a daily news website for her small town, and many people read it.
lessons.text:
Linda lived in Pine Hill, a small town in Oregon. Pine Hill had no local news website. People in Pine Hill didn't know much about the news of their own town.

Linda had an idea. She wanted to launch a news website for the town. She had a computer, a phone and a lot of free time.

First, Linda went to a conference about local news in Portland. At the conference, she learned how to write short news stories. She also learned how to make good content for the internet. "Good content is short, simple and true," one person at the conference said.

Back home, Linda worked at her computer every day. She wrote about the new school, the high school football team and the town's shops.

In March, Linda launched the website. She called it "Pine Hill Daily." And the news really was daily: every morning, she published 2 new stories.

The stories were short. When something changed, Linda wrote an update. One day, the road to the lake was closed. Linda published an update at 9 and another update at 12.

Linda also did interviews. Her first interview was with the oldest woman in town. The woman was 101 years old. In the interview, she talked about life in Pine Hill 80 years ago. Many people read the interview and shared it on the internet.

After 1 month, the website had 2,000 users. Users wrote comments about recent news. Some users sent Linda ideas for new stories. "Can you do an interview with the new teacher?" one user asked.

Linda was very happy. A recent message from a user said, "Thank you, Linda. Now we know the news of our own town."

Questions:
What did Linda want to launch?
She wanted to launch a news website for the town.
Where did Linda go first?
She went to a conference about local news in Portland.
How many new stories were published every morning?
2 new stories were published every morning.
What did Linda do when something changed?
She wrote an update.
Who was the first interview with?
Her first interview was with the oldest woman in town.
How many users did the website have after 1 month?
The website had 2,000 users.

lessons.title: 1,000 Boxes
lessons.summary: Maria and the food bank find enough food to pack 1,000 boxes for families.
lessons.text:
Every Saturday, Maria helped at the food bank in her town. The food bank gave free food to families with little money.

In November, the food bank had a problem. There was a lack of food. The stock was very low. There was also a lack of people to help.

Tom was a worker at the food bank. He talked to Maria. "Our stock is too low," he said. "We need a new supply of food before Thanksgiving. Our target is 1,000 boxes for 1,000 families."

Maria had an idea. She called a partner of the food bank: a big store on Main Street. The store was an old partner, and the manager wanted to help. "We can send a big supply of food on Friday," he said.

In addition, Maria asked the schools for help. The children brought food from home. She also wrote a message to her friends: "Can you help us pack boxes on Saturday?"

On Friday, the supply from the store arrived. It arrived at 8 in the morning. Later that day, the food from the schools arrived too. Now the stock was big.

On Saturday, 40 people came to help. Tom and the other workers showed them how to pack a box. They packed food for 1 week in each box. Everyone packed box after box.

At 5, Tom counted the boxes. There were 1,000 boxes. "We hit our target!" he said. Everyone was very happy.

The next week, the food bank fed 1,000 families. "We can feed every family on our list," Tom said. "In addition, we have stock for December." Maria was happy. She helped feed her town.

Questions:
What was the problem at the food bank?
There was a lack of food, and the stock was very low.
What was the target?
The target was 1,000 boxes for 1,000 families.
Who did Maria call?
She called a partner of the food bank, a big store on Main Street.
When did the supply from the store arrive?
It arrived on Friday at 8 in the morning.
What did the people do on Saturday?
They packed food for 1 week in each box.
How many families did the food bank feed?
The food bank fed 1,000 families.

lessons.title: The Big Game
lessons.summary: Jake, the fastest player on the town team, helps the Hawks win a huge game.
lessons.text:
Jake was 17 years old. He played football for the Riverton Hawks, the high school team of his small town. Jake wore number ten. Everyone in town knew number ten. He was the fastest player on the team, and everyone talked about his speed.

In November, the Hawks had a huge game against the Lakeview Bears. The Bears were the best team in the state. They were big and strong. Before the game, some players on the Hawks felt fear. "Don't let fear win," the coach said. "Play your game."

On Friday night, every seat at the field was full. People came from every street in town. There wasn't a single free seat. It was a huge night for Riverton.

The game was a battle. The Bears were strong, but the Hawks were fast. After the first half, the Bears had ten points and the Hawks had ten points too. In the second half, the battle continued. Late in the game, the score was 17 to 17.

With 1 minute left, the ball went to Jake. He used all his speed. He ran past 1 player, then past 2 players. In the last minute, the fans stood up and counted the seconds. "10, 9, 8, 7..." they counted. With 5 seconds left, Jake crossed the goal line. The Hawks won 24 to 17.

The fans went crazy. Jake's mother and father ran to him. "You had no fear!" his father said.

After the game, the coach talked to the team. "This is a big success," he said. "But it is not the success of 1 player. It is the success of the whole team and the whole town."

Questions:
What number did Jake wear?
Jake wore number ten.
What did everyone talk about?
Everyone talked about his speed.
How was the field on Friday night?
Every seat at the field was full.
What was the score with 1 minute left?
The score was 17 to 17.
What did the fans do in the last minute?
They stood up and counted the seconds.
What did the coach say after the game?
He said that it was the success of the whole team and the whole town.

lessons.title: The Fish House
lessons.summary: Rosa and her husband open a fish restaurant in an old building, and it becomes popular.
lessons.text:
Rosa and her husband, Carlos, lived in Bayport, a small town by the sea. Rosa loved to cook fish. Her husband loved to talk to people. They had a dream: to open their own fish restaurant.

On Main Street, there was an old building. It was built in 1920. For 10 years, nobody used it. The owner of the building wanted to sell it. Rosa and Carlos met the owner. "This is a great spot," Carlos said. "It's near the sea and near the shops." They bought the building. Now they were the owners.

The building was old, so they made it modern inside. They put in new tables, new chairs and modern lights. In the front, they built a big window. From the window, people could see the sea.

Above the door, Carlos put a sign: "Welcome to the Fish House."

On the first day, Carlos stood at the door. He welcomed every person. "Welcome! Welcome to the Fish House!" he said. Rosa cooked fresh fish from the sea. On hot days, people also loved her cold drinks.

Soon the Fish House was popular. Families came on weekends. Workers from the shops came after work. The best spot was the table by the window. Everyone wanted that spot.

After 1 year, the Fish House was the most popular place on Main Street. Rosa and Carlos were happy owners. "We built our dream," Rosa said to her husband.

Questions:
Where did Rosa and her husband live?
They lived in Bayport, a small town by the sea.
When was the old building built?
It was built in 1920.
What did Carlos say about the building?
He said that it was a great spot.
What did they build in the front?
They built a big window.
What was the best spot in the Fish House?
The best spot was the table by the window.
What did Rosa say to her husband?
She said, "We built our dream."

lessons.title: Music in the Park
lessons.summary: Emma and her brother go to a free concert in the park and have a great night.
lessons.text:
Every summer, the town of Greenville had free music in the park on Friday nights. This Friday, a local band was going to play. The band was called The Blue Birds.

In the morning, Emma read about it on the town website. "A local band is playing in the park tonight," it said. "It starts at 7 and finishes at 9. Bring your family!"

Emma asked her brother, Ben, "Shall we go tonight?" "Yes, let's go," Ben said.

At 6, Emma put on her favorite summer dress. Soon she was dressed and ready. Ben was not ready. "Shall I wait for you?" she asked. "Yes, please. I'll be ready in 5 minutes," he said.

The park was full. The host of the night was Mike, a teacher from the high school. Mike was very funny. He told funny stories about the town, and everyone laughed. Emma laughed a lot. "He is so funny," she said to Ben.

Next to the stage, there were pictures by local artists. One artist made beautiful pictures of the river. Another artist made pictures of old houses in Greenville.

Then the host said, "And now, the band!" The band played old songs and new songs. The singer of the band was also an artist. Some of the pictures were her work.

At 9, the singer said, "We always finish with a love song. This is our last song tonight." "Shall we dance?" Ben asked. Emma laughed. "Yes!" They danced with the other families.

After the last song, the host said, "Thank you, everyone! The band was super tonight!" On the way home, Emma said, "That was a super night. Let's come again next Friday."

Questions:
What did Emma ask her brother?
She asked, "Shall we go tonight?"
What did Emma put on?
She put on her favorite summer dress.
Who was the host of the night?
The host was Mike, a teacher from the high school.
Why did everyone laugh?
Mike told funny stories about the town.
What did one artist make?
One artist made beautiful pictures of the river.
What did the host say at the end?
He said, "The band was super tonight!"

lessons.title: Help for Frank
lessons.summary: Frank hurts his back, and Leo, the boy next door, does his shopping for 6 weeks.
lessons.text:
Frank was 78 years old. He lived alone on Elm Street. One day in winter, he carried a heavy box, and he hurt his back. His back hurt a lot.

Frank went to the hospital. The doctor gave him treatment for his back. "The treatment takes 6 weeks," the doctor said. "Don't carry any weight. No heavy weight at all."

At home, life was difficult. It was difficult to walk to the shop. It was difficult to carry food home. Frank simply couldn't do his shopping.

Leo was 12 years old. He lived next door with his mother. One day, he saw Frank at the window. "Can I help you, sir?" Leo asked.

"Thank you, young man," Frank said. "I hurt my back, and I can't handle the shopping now. I can't handle any weight."

"I can handle it," Leo said. "I promise. I can go to the shop for you every day after school."

"That is very kind," Frank said. "Can you start tomorrow?"

"Yes, sir. I can start tomorrow after school."

The next day, Leo came at 4. He took Frank's list and went to the shop. He carried everything home. He did it every day for 6 weeks. It was not always easy, but he kept his promise.

After 6 weeks, the treatment was over. Frank's back was better now. He could carry things again.

"Leo, you kept your promise every day," Frank said. "You simply made my life easy. Tomorrow, I want to make a big lunch for you and your mother."

"Thank you, sir," Leo said. He was very happy.

Questions:
How did Frank hurt his back?
He carried a heavy box, and he hurt his back.
What did the doctor say?
The doctor said, "Don't carry any weight."
Why was life difficult for Frank?
It was difficult to walk to the shop and carry food home.
What did Leo promise?
He promised to go to the shop for Frank every day after school.
Did Leo keep his promise?
Yes, he kept his promise every day for 6 weeks.
What did Frank want to do for Leo?
He wanted to make a big lunch for Leo and his mother.

lessons.title: Trees for Main Street
lessons.summary: Anna and the street association plant 60 trees on a hot, wide street.
lessons.text:
Anna lived on Main Street in Fairview. The street was wide, but it had no trees. In summer, it was very hot. Every summer, the heat seemed to rise.

Anna was a member of the Main Street Association. At a meeting of the association, she shared an idea. "In many towns, there is a movement to plant trees," she said. "Let's join the movement. Let's plant trees on Main Street." Everyone liked the idea.

First, they needed a plan. Anna's friend Tom knew a lot about trees. He explained the method. "The method is simple," he said. "First, we measure the street. Then we plant a tree every 30 feet. We plant the trees in 2 straight lines, 1 line on each side of the street."

On Saturday, 20 people came. They measured the street from one end to the other. The street was very wide. They marked a spot for each tree.

Next, they made holes for the trees. Tom explained, "The roots of a tree grow below the ground. The roots need space below the ground to develop. In the first year, a young tree develops its roots. Then it grows above the ground."

They worked all day, and the heat started to rise. At the end of the day, there were 60 young trees on Main Street, in 2 straight lines.

The next morning, Anna got up when the sun started to rise. She walked down Main Street. She looked at the young trees. "In a few years, this wide street is going to be green and cool," she said. She was happy to be a part of the movement.

Questions:
What was the problem on Main Street?
The street was wide, but it had no trees, and it was very hot.
What did Anna say at the meeting of the association?
She said, "Let's join the movement. Let's plant trees on Main Street."
What was the first step of the method?
The first step was to measure the street.
How did they plant the trees?
They planted the trees in 2 straight lines.
Why do the roots need space below the ground?
They need space below the ground to develop.
How many trees were on Main Street at the end of the day?
There were 60 young trees on Main Street.

lessons.title: A Job for Amir
lessons.summary: Amir, new to the town, gets help from his neighbor and an agency and finds a job.
lessons.text:
Amir and his wife, Sara, came to Clearwater from a foreign country. Everything was new for them: the language, the food and the money. Amir spoke some English, but it was difficult for him.

Karen lived in the house next to them. She welcomed them to the street. One day, Karen asked Amir about his life. Amir told her the truth.

"To tell the truth, we have financial problems," he said. "I currently don't have a job. We have little money, and there is a lot of financial pressure on us."

"First, you need legal papers to work," Karen said. "There is an agency in town. The agency helps foreign families. Let's go there together."

At the agency, a woman named Nora helped Amir. She checked his papers. "Everything is legal," she said. "You can work in this country." Then Nora looked at her computer. "A store on Main Street currently needs a sales associate. I can refer you to the manager."

Nora referred Amir to the store. The manager gave him a job application. Karen helped him with the English words on the application. Then Amir gave the application to the manager.

The next week, Amir had an interview with the manager. He felt a lot of pressure, but he told the truth. "In my country, I worked in a shop for 10 years," he said. The manager liked him.

On Monday, Amir started work as a sales associate. He was a good associate, and the customers liked him. The financial pressure was smaller now.

"Thank you, Karen," Amir said. "The truth is, we feel at home now."

Questions:
Where did Amir and Sara come from?
They came from a foreign country.
What did Amir tell Karen?
He told her the truth: they had financial problems, and he didn't have a job.
What does the agency do?
The agency helps foreign families.
What did Nora say about the papers?
She said, "Everything is legal."
Who helped Amir with the application?
Karen helped him with the English words on the application.
What job did Amir get?
He got a job as a sales associate at a store on Main Street.

lessons.title: The Block Party
lessons.summary: Jen plans a summer party on Maple Street, and the whole street comes.
lessons.text:
Every year in July, the people on Maple Street had a block party. This year, Jen planned the party. She started 3 weeks in advance. "A good party needs a plan in advance," she said.

Jen sent a message to every house on the street. "Please tell me in advance what you can bring," she wrote.

Dan wrote back, "I can bring my gas grill and make hot dogs." Lily wrote, "I can bring hot dog rolls and cold drinks." Sam wrote, "I have an old ice cream machine. Can I bring my machine?" "Yes, of course!" Jen answered.

The day before the party, Dan checked the gas in his grill. There was enough gas for the whole day. On the day of the party, Dan started to make the hot dogs. But the first hot dogs burned. "Oh no, I burned them!" Dan said, and everyone laughed. After that, nothing burned.

Lily put the hot dogs in the rolls. She had 200 rolls. People also loved her cold drinks.

The children went crazy for Sam's machine. They stood in a long line for ice cream. Some children rolled a big ball down the street. Others played music and danced.

The party was a nice mix of people: children, parents and old people, old families and new families. Some people didn't know each other before. At the party, they started to mix and talk.

At 9, Jen counted the people. There were 120 people. "This is crazy," she said. "This is the best block party ever!"

Questions:
When did Jen start to plan the party?
She started 3 weeks in advance.
What did Dan bring?
He brought his gas grill.
What happened to the first hot dogs?
The first hot dogs burned.
What did Lily bring?
She brought hot dog rolls and cold drinks.
What did the children go crazy for?
They went crazy for Sam's ice cream machine.
Who came to the party?
It was a mix of people: children, parents and old people.
